chunks: Al-Hasan ibn Muhammad ibn Yahya al-Alawi (may Allah have mercy on him) told us, saying: My grandfather told me, saying: Dawud ibn al-Qasim told us, saying: Isa informed us, saying: Yusuf ibn Ya'qoub informed us, saying: 'Anbasa told us, from 'Amr ibn Dinar, from 'Ikrima, saying:

When Fatima (peace be upon her) gave birth to Hasan, she brought him to the Prophet, and he named him Hasan. And when she gave birth to al-Husayn, she brought him to him and said: O Messenger of Allah, this one is more beautiful than that one, so he named him Husayn.

key_terms.حُسَيْنًا: Husayn, a diminutive form of Hasan, meaning 'the little beautiful one'
key_terms.فَاطِمُ عَلَيْهَا السَّلَامُ: Fatima (peace be upon her), daughter of the Prophet

ai.seo_question: What is the origin and meaning of the names Hasan and Husayn according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This narration from Shaykh al-Saduq’s *Ma'ani al-Akhbar* underscores the linguistic wisdom behind the names Hasan and Husayn, linking the latter to the root 'h-s-n' (beauty) as a divine attribute. It reflects the Shia tradition of recognizing the Prophet’s intuitive naming based on the infants' inherent qualities, reinforcing the spiritual stature of the Ahl al-Bayt within the early Islamic community.
